# Capture applications from a form

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers drip-campaigns work end to end across Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. New Email Form Submission
2. Score the Lead
3. Assign Round-Robin Owner
4. Route by Heat
5. Hot → Google Sheets + Instant Ping
6. Notify Assigned Owner
7. Warm → Drip via Microsoft Teams
8. Cold → Park in Nurture List
9. Combine Lead Paths

## Why it exists

Doing drip-campaigns work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Email Form Submission → Score the Lead → Assign Round-Robin Owner → Route by Heat → Hot → Google Sheets + Instant Ping → Notify Assigned Owner → Warm → Drip via Microsoft Teams → Cold → Park in Nurture List → Combine Lead Paths

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams aligned by hand for drip campaigns
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Google Sheets, for drip campaigns
- Drip campaigns work where "Score the Lead" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Drip campaigns work that only reaches Google Sheets when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Microsoft Teams in step for drip campaigns, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or Microsoft Teams call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this drip-campaigns build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a drip-campaigns run reports once rather than 9 times
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for drip campaigns before wiring Google Sheets
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for drip campaigns

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Round-robin owner assignment happens right after scoring, before routing — every lead gets an accountable owner regardless of tier, so even a 'cold' lead parked in the nurture list is someone's responsibility later, not an anonymous row in a spreadsheet.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Change the hot/warm threshold values and watch the tier distribution shift.
2. Add a 4th owner to the round-robin pool.
3. Add a follow-up wait+check to the warm-drip branch, similar to the drip-ladder spine.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your drip campaigns process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

**Do not log**
drip-campaigns payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
